rounds.proof_sketch: blockDim.z=1 vs blockDim.x=256. Original: (256+31)/32=8 warps read. Mutated: (1+31)/32=1 warp read. Warps 1-7 products replaced with 1.0, losing their contributions to final product.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutant survived initial testing likely due to random chance or specific value distributions. The mutation changes the warp count threshold from 8 to 1, causing 7 warp products to be replaced with 1.0 in the final reduction. This fundamentally breaks the multi-warp reduction for any block size > 32 threads, but requires non-unity input values to manifest as a detectable difference.
rounds.kill_strategy: Use constant non-unity values (e.g., 0.99) across the entire input tensor. The original will compute 0.99^N for all elements along the reduction dimension, while the mutant will only include ~1/8 of those multiplications, yielding 0.99^(N/8) instead—a difference that grows exponentially with reduction_size.
rounds.recommendations: When using warp/block dimension variables in conditional logic (like determining number of warps), always validate against the actual launch configuration. Add assertions that verify blockDim.z is intentionally used when accessed, or use named constants to avoid index confusion.
